beats.caption: 3D NAND stacks the cells: tall towers of word-line layers
beats.text: Modern NAND builds its cells in a vertical stack of dozens to hundreds of layers, with a channel hole running through them. Each layer's gate is one cell's control gate on that layer.

beats.caption: Cut through: electrons caught in traps in a nitride film
beats.text: A charge-trap cell replaces the conductive floating gate with a silicon nitride film full of defects. Electrons park in these traps, and the film is continuous, so charge stays local to its trap.

beats.caption: One defect holds a few electrons; a leak drains only that spot
beats.text: Because the charge is local, a single defect in the film does not drain the whole cell. That makes the cell more robust than a floating gate and lets the cells sit closer together.

beats.caption: Used in most high-layer 3D NAND
beats.text: Many 3D NAND products use this structure for their high layer counts, since the stacked layers are easier to make with a continuous film than with isolated poly islands.

beats.caption: Makers: Samsung, SK Hynix, Kioxia, Lam Research (LRCX)
beats.text: Samsung (005930.KS), SK Hynix (000660.KS), Kioxia (285A.T) and Lam Research (LRCX) (deposition and etch tools) make and enable these stacks.
